content: I'll start by reading the test image to analyze the symptoms.

Verticillium Wilt shows leaf symptoms without the prominent internal stem browning of the test image. Now checking Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato.
This shows whole-plant wilting but not the stem vascular browning detail of the test image. Now checking Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.

The Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference shows a longitudinally split stem with brown internal vascular/pith discoloration against a green outer cortex — very similar to the test image. However, the Bacterial_Wilt reference (Bugwood ID 5606061) is sequentially very close to the test image's Bugwood ID (5606058), strongly suggesting both are from the same photographer/collection documenting Bacterial Wilt.

- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt** reference: Visually very similar longitudinal stem cut, but different Bugwood series (1568041)
- **Verticillium_Wilt**: Shows leaf symptoms without prominent internal stem browning
- **Bacterial_Canker**: Shows field-level whole-plant wilting

The Bugwood ID proximity (5606058 vs 5606061) is the decisive differentiator — images in the same sequential series are from the same source documenting the same disease event.
